scope: Second architecture review after reconciliation, against local feature contracts; no host capability certification

findings.title: Remove plan-only validation from spec creation
findings.finding: The spec new procedure requires validating/recording target_branch, resolving --comparison-base, and rejecting abandoned plan dependencies. None is an input to spec new; this paragraph duplicates plan new. Implementing it literally introduces undefined inputs or plan prerequisites to ordinary spec creation.
findings.recommendation: Remove the copied plan-specific sentences from spec new; retain them in plan new. Check spec creation against its own feature inputs.

findings.title: Define the snapshot used for transactional index generation
findings.finding: Generation reads only already committed plans/config, but shelve/resume and plan approve edit lifecycle metadata, regenerate, and commit metadata plus index together. Reading HEAD during this sequence emits the old status. The same ambiguity affects regeneration while resolving a merge before a merged commit exists.
findings.recommendation: Specify a deterministic explicit prospective snapshot for transaction/merge generation, distinct from standalone committed-snapshot lookup, and explain how it satisfies the committed-index contract. Test approval, shelving/resume and pre-commit merge resolution for byte-identical post-commit regeneration.

findings.title: Reconcile completed-step reruns with recording refusals
findings.finding: The feature and conductor contract allow explicit --step N --force --reason TEXT completed-step reruns and require recording through step-done. Its input contract omits --reason and unconditionally refuses done/skipped steps and appending an earlier step after a later handoff section. Force is only described as overriding the blocked-step guard. A permitted rerun therefore cannot be recorded by the specified shared recorder.
findings.recommendation: Define the explicit rerun recording mode, required reason and audit trailer, narrowly qualified completed-step/history exceptions, and preserved earlier HANDOFF sections. Retain all lease, edit-set and lifecycle guards. Test an earlier completed-step rerun after later steps have been recorded.
